Every product.image AND every entry in images[] starts with https://customer-assets.emergentagent.com/ — zero unsplash.com / pexels.com references. lung-punch-hoodie returns total_supply=500/sold_count=218; graffiti-hoodie returns 400/247; lung-punch-vinyl returns 1000/387. Navbar logo renders 'BEATS BY DEZ. THE STORE'. Footer shows '© 2026 BeatsByDez. All rights reserved.' (visible in screenshot — DOM splits © and year across spans so a simple regex doesn't match the whole phrase, but rendered text is correct). Home hero eyebrow reads '▸ NEW DROP / BEATSBYDEZ'. Shop subheader contains "Straight from Dez's catalog". Product detail trust badge reads 'Authentic merch direct from Dez'. All 6 new merch product cards (lung-punch-hoodie/crew/tee, graffiti-hoodie/tee, beats-by-dez-cap) render real customer-asset images on /shop. Full smoke flow lung-punch-hoodie size L → cart → /checkout → POST /api/orders → /order/SM-F14B13B6 confirmation page (subtotal $95.00, shipping $9.99, total $104.99) — clean, no console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:309 — order_number prefix is still 'SM-' (legacy from Sony Music). Functional / non-blocking, but inconsistent with the BeatsByDez rebrand. Consider renaming prefix to 'BBD-' or 'DEZ-' for full brand consistency.

server.py:231-241 — startup seed still hard-deletes and reinserts products & artists on every backend boot. This wipes drop_ends_at every reboot (countdowns reset) and would also wipe any future user-edited inventory. OK for demo, but flag for production hardening.

server.py — beats-by-dez-cap uses LUNG_PUNCH_MERCH as its image (flatlay shows the hoodie, not a cap). Functionally a customer-asset (passes the no-stock-photo rule), but visually mislabeled — a cap product card showing a hoodie photo is a UX risk. Recommend either uploading a real cap photo or relabeling the asset.

Similarly lung-punch-crew and lung-punch-tee reuse the same LUNG_PUNCH_MERCH flatlay as lung-punch-hoodie — all three apparel cards render the identical image on /shop. Not a bug, but visually confusing for shoppers comparing variants.
